title: Do You Project the Identity You Want To
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This entry urges leaders to be deliberate about the small set of identities — such as strong, caring, or strategic — that they most want others to perceive in them, rather than leaving that impression to chance. It cautions against trying to project too many favorable traits at once and instead recommends narrowing to three or four core qualities. The real work, the piece argues, is checking whether daily behaviors under stress actually reflect the chosen identity, since people draw conclusions from action rather than stated values. It closes by reminding leaders that others will respond to who they appear to be, regardless of internal self-perception.
points: People constantly draw conclusions about a leader's character from their actions, whether the leader intends it or not.
Leaders are urged to narrow their desired self-image to three or four core qualities rather than an exhaustive list.
Values and projected identity aren't the same thing and should be examined separately.
Behavior under stress and pressure is the real test of whether an identity is actually being projected.
quotes: The identity a leader projects influences how people respond to them.
Decide exactly what is most important for you to be seen as.
Don’t confuse what you value and what identity you want others to conclude about you.
Just because you value and believe you are compassionate doesn’t mean you act compassionately in the eyes of others.
The good news is that no one can project a false image over time.
Remember, people will respond and engage based upon who they see you to be, not who you believe you are.
